resolutions.researcher_notes: Status 'operating' confirmed by two independent sources. EGAS (official Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co) history timeline: 'Start of Arab Gas Pipeline operations — Egypt's first natural gas export pipeline project' (2003) and 'Resumption of gas exports to Jordan via the Arab Gas Pipeline after a four-year halt' (2019). Attaqa (Nov 2024) describes the line still carrying gas: Egypt-Jordan flow resumed 2018 after Zohr, and Israeli gas flowing through it to Jordan since 2020, with Arish as the junction point. Syrian Observer (2021, verified live) 'Arab Gas Pipeline Ready, Syria Gets Egyptian Gas' further corroborates. The two current refs (kingabdullah.jo inauguration + attaqa) were flagged DEAD_LINK in the brief but both re-verify live (200); the Egyptian Arish-Taba segment is the operating export feeder.

VALUE CONTRADICTION FLAGGED. The current ref hydrocarbons-technology.com now 301-redirects to offshore-technology.com/projects/arab-gas-pipeline-agp/ (same content, live). That page states: 'The first phase (Arish-Aqaba section), commissioned in July 2003 at an investment of $220m' — corroborating the year (2003) and USD unit, but giving $220,000,000, NOT the GEM value $207,550,000. The $220m consistently appears across mirrors (Wikipedia, oilgasstoragenews, oilandgasadvancement) but all trace to the same offshore-technology profile, so this is effectively a single independent origin (independent=false). No source anywhere states $207.55m exactly. Possible reconciliation: $220m is the full Arish-Aqaba first phase (250km overland Arish-Taba + 15km subsea Taba-Aqaba + compressor/metering stations); GEM's $207.55m may be an overland-Arish-Taba-only subset, but this is unverified. Recommend Update review the SegmentCost figure against the source's $220m.

Operator 'Egyptian Natural Gas Co' (GASCO) confirmed by two independent sources. EGAS official history: 'Establishment of the Egyptian Natural Gas Company (GASCO) as the Transmission System Operator (TSO)' (1997) — GASCO is Egypt's national gas transmission operator. Offshore-technology AGP profile names 'the Egyptian Natural Gas Company (GASCO)' in the first-phase consortium and states the Egyptian section is operated by GASCO and EGAS under the Ministry of Petroleum. Both support GASCO = Egyptian Natural Gas Co as operator of the Arish-Taba Egyptian segment.
